scope: Read-only five adaptation modules + primary original source. Reuses root431endpoint audit; does not repeat core/data consistency audits.
headline: CGR-to-palm algebra is consistent with the declared Boya convention. Main fidelity gap is learned ranking AFTER CGR/geometry/arm first-admitted compression, rather than BEFORE post-processing. Hand reference and closure are Boya approximations, not original-hand hardware reproduction.

findings.conclusion: Paper: top100CGR x types -> learned scores -> top200 collision -> highest remaining. Official DH3 code: CGRtop1000 -> all4type x4extra scoring/gather -> top3500/score>.85 -> mapped poses -> scoretop400 -> collision -> final highest. Boya: each fixed gesture/extra cell CGRtop500 -> first8geometry-admitted across2flips -> at most4arm plans -> first admitted only -> learned rerank78 external plans. This irreversibly removes alternative seed/flip/aperture placements before the learned head sees them. Current6/10 is a same-admitted-pool comparison, not full-deployment success.
findings.limits: Paper/code topK differ; both put learned ranking ahead of hand collision. Full-deployment connection is necessary before claiming faithful deployment, but does not invalidate the narrower paired experiment.

findings.conclusion: T_Wpalm=T_Wcamera*T_cameraCGR*[R_cgr_ref, (raw_depth+extra)*e_x]*inverse(T_palm_ref). R_cgr_ref=[e_y,e_z,e_x] is proper; rawdepth and extra are added once along CGR+X. Additional0/10/20/30mm matches original extra-depth choice. No source DH35mm-backoff or Inspire/Allegro14mm offset is blindly transferred. These offsets are hand-specific, so omission is intentional Boya datum choice, not proven depth bug.
findings.limits: Root zero-physics audit431 mappings max endpoint error2.30555e-16m is reused, not rerun. Exact intended contact plane for Boya still requires calibration; algebraic correctness is not grasp-quality proof.

findings.conclusion: Original mapping tables are per-opening, per-type selected contact-mesh landmarks: DH3 common/pose3 use thumb-vs-average-two-opponent midpoint; pose2 uses opponent-pair midpoint. Thus preshape contact midpoint itself has original precedent; original source does NOT establish universal closure-invariant capture center. Boya uniformly uses generic source five_finger_wrap distal th-versus-single-ff pads, a thumb-tangent approach, and both closures move toward fixed template nominal at fixed palm. Asymmetric closure can shift the free-space pad midpoint substantially; it is a plausible limitation, not proof of mis-signed pose or cause of four failures.
findings.limits: Some source family contact annotations differ: packageg1 ff contact is ffmiddle whereas adapter chooses generic ffdistal. This is declared geometric-reference replacement, not an accidental FK mismatch. Do not claim replacing open midpoint by closed midpoint is author-required or guaranteed correct.

findings.conclusion: Official collision detector expands two-finger width by1.7, then hand mapper clamps per-type width domain. Boya likewise expands once then clips to33sample self-collision-clear th/ff reference distances and accepts nearest slot within2mm. Factor/clamp logic has source precedent. Boya reference_width is a pad distance, not maximum mechanical aperture or physical free gap; finite slot spacing and clamping are new calibration assumptions.
findings.limits: Root431audit reports226clamped. Of4learned failures3are clamped, but no controlled comparison establishes causality; many successful candidates are clamped too.

findings.conclusion: Both original and Boya flip R[:,1:3] by -1 (180deg about approach). Original chooses one camera-frame sign to avoid arm boundary; Boya enumerates both orientations and binds actual bool. prepare_binding reuses original get_graspgroup_features once on original raw2261 + actualflip, including opposite half-swap and angle rotation. No double canonicalization found. Boya base jaw reference puts thumb on CGR-Y, whereas DH3 common frame tool_y points toward selected thumb landmark; this fixed handedness is a hand-table convention that freshly trained Boya heads can learn, not use of DH3 pretrained scoring weights.
findings.limits: Enumerating both and deterministic tie-breaking are deployment adaptations, not literal original sign policy. Source if_flip differs from official_policy_if_flip by design and is correctly recorded.

findings.conclusion: Official uses pre-shaped hand voxel versus partial scene with5cm collision approach checks; paper describes10cm pregrasp and UR planner, then hardware force-limited closure. Boya uses full source-link hulls, analytic table0.5mm,21samples over10cm, full-arm IK/path gates, and fixed open-to-company-nominal position commands through existing Isaac backend. No original hardware feedback/force70 or learned closure policy is recreated. Wrist values remain source template and arm targets palm; supplied world_object_pose preserves hand/object relation, not a second candidate rotation.
findings.limits: Contact can stop actual fingers under finite drives while targets continue. Nominal no-contact pad endpoints alone do not establish actual object retention or hardware equivalence.
